attempts.summary: Deployed PostgreSQL 9.5 streaming replication across node1 (initial primary), node2, and node3 (standbys) using pg_basebackup + recovery.conf. Demonstrated failover by stopping node1: promoted node2 to writable primary with zero data loss, repointed node3 to replicate from node2, then rebuilt node1 as a standby of node2 via fresh base backup. Final steady state: node2 = primary, node1 & node3 = streaming standbys, all data consistent. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol on all three nodes one at a time (node1, node3, then node2-the-current-primary-last), each showing a changed boot_id/uptime and full replication/data recovery afterward, with quorum/write-availability preserved throughout (never restarting the sole writable primary until the topology no longer depended on the just-restarted nodes for availability).
